clue.text: Refuse to believe CID's tried to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters before it must be put into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's still gives an S here: CID plus S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Detectives from the CID are being urged to mend their ways, and someone refuses to believe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges CIDS and TRIED together; the 's of CID's is counted as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to reject it as untrue, which is refusing to believe it.

clue.text: Knock up quick runs coming in totally without fear

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole run is read from the bottom up

parts.note: quick means alive, as in the quick and the dead

indicators.note: coming in means a piece enters inside another

parts.note: dead as in dead right means totally
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman knocks up quick runs and plays entirely without fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock up' and 'quick runs' paint cricket practice; in a down clue 'up' reverses the lot, LIVE plus DERAD (R put in by 'coming in') becoming the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil person is reckless and bold, ready to take any risk.

clue.text: Filthy home of covert wet

indicators.note: covert means hidden or covered, so the word of is concealed inside the other piece

parts.note: a sty is a pig's dirty home
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dirty den where secret agents dwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' is a noun here: a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet is a feeble, weak-willed person, a weakling.

clue.text: Joint sprained we're told is handicap

indicators.note: we're told says we hear the words rather than see them spelt

parts.note: the wrist is a joint, and ricked means sprained

explanation.surface: A sprained joint is described as a handicap.
explanation.definitionFit: To handicap is to hamper or limit, which is to constrain someone.

clue.text: Representative given instruction to remove barrier

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark meaning delete
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: An envoy is told to take down a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is someone sent to act or speak on behalf of others.

clue.text: Point to neck and shoulder covering

parts.note: a tip is a point
to neck is to kiss and cuddle, to pet

explanation.surface: Someone gestures toward the neck and a shawl over the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippet is a scarf or cape worn round the shoulders.

clue.text: Stroke fawn

definitions.meaning: a swimming stroke, the fast overarm front stroke
to fawn is to grovel or toady

explanation.definitionFit: Front crawl is a swimming stroke, and to grovel before someone is to creep and flatter them.

clue.text: May commanding officer turn up for a drink?

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue says the whole run is flipped to read upwards

parts.note: may, as in may I, means can
GOC is General Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: Might the commanding officer arrive in time for a drink?
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month or a name; it is CAN. GOC is the army's General Officer Commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a spirit one drinks.

clue.text: The last word namely, in its facilities

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
IE, id est, means namely

explanation.surface: The final say rests, in a sense, with its facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful features or services of a place, its conveniences.

clue.text: Leaders of losing armies take early retirement afterwards

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, taken from each of the following words

explanation.surface: Commanders of defeated forces step down early.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, which is what afterwards means.

clue.text: Fur seal destroyed? No

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fur seal has been killed, and the answer is no.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a negative reply, a no to a request.

clue.text: People who watch large black and white set finally get colour

parts.words: People who watch large black and white
parts.note: Large Black and Large White are breeds of pig, and those who tend pigs are pigmen

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word set

explanation.surface: Viewers of a big black-and-white television eventually get a colour set.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests old television sets; in fact Large Black and Large White are British pig breeds, so their keepers are PIGMEN; 'finally' adds T, the last letter of 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour, so it can stand for a colour.

clue.text: Horse doctor swallowing whiskey

indicators.note: swallowing means one piece takes another down inside it

parts.note: rye is a whiskey distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: A vet is drinking whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse doctor' reads as a vet, but 'Horse' alone is the definition: a clothes horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a frame for airing laundry, a kind of clothes dryer.

clue.text: Soldier regained rank? Right

indicators.note: rank here means foul or corrupt, so the word before it is spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier asks whether he has got his rank back, and is told he has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like military rank but is the anagram signal on REGAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is an infantry soldier, originally one who threw grenades.

clue.text: High spirits when exam has taken place — that could be capital

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination, as for a degree
a capital is a city, so a city is something that could be a capital

explanation.surface: A student is in high spirits once the exam is over, and the capital is the place to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivacity is liveliness and animation, which is what high spirits are.

clue.text: Having moved, I've sublet the hall

indicators.note: having moved means the letters have been shifted about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant who has moved out has let the hall to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestibule is an entrance hall or lobby.

clue.text: Quickly repaired shelter, say

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the word and take its sound

parts.note: a hide is a hidden shelter used to watch birds or game

explanation.surface: A shelter was patched up in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' means went (to repair to a place), not mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Hied is an old word for hastened, and to repair somewhere is to go there.

clue.text: Discovered in falsehood, is char getting sack?

indicators.note: discovered in means the letters are found lying within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Caught in a lie, will the cleaning lady be fired?
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a cleaning woman, a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge an employee is to dismiss them from a job.

clue.text: Only one warrant officer around to make mistake

parts.note: sole means only

indicators.note: around means the second piece is wrapped about the first

parts.note: a CSM, company sergeant major, is a warrant officer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Only one warrant officer is on hand, which invites errors.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is an error, especially in grammar or etiquette.

clue.text: For instance, German communist gets on top of problem

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting on top of means one piece is placed above the other

parts.note: COM is short for communist
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A German communist gets the better of a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is not nationality: Sir Edward German was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward German wrote light operas, so he is one example of a musical writer.

clue.text: Survive, after all

definitions.meaning: to survive is to endure or hold out
coming after all the others, final

explanation.definitionFit: To endure or keep going is a meaning of the verb, and coming after every other one means final.

clue.text: Business with deficit — American giant

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a deficit is a loss
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An American giant of business is running at a deficit.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a huge statue or person, a giant in size or importance.

clue.text: Charges gunmen caught up in quarrel

indicators.note: caught means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the piece is read upward, backwards

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners

explanation.surface: Gunmen are caught up in a quarrel and charges follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a list of charges or a duty levied.

clue.text: Several birds

definitions.meaning: an old word for various or several

explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means sundry, and loons are waterbirds named for diving.

clue.text: No officer around is free from state control

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a private is a soldier with no officer's rank
taken as written

explanation.surface: No officer is around, so the unit is free from state control.
explanation.definitionFit: To privatise an industry is to transfer it out of public ownership to private hands.

clue.text: Force to serve jam

definitions.meaning: to force them into the navy
to jam is to squeeze or cram

explanation.definitionFit: Press gangs conscripted men into naval service, and cramming something tight is squeezing it.

clue.text: Park in station

definitions.meaning: to park something is to set it down or place it, as one sets up a tent
a trader's or busker's regular spot

explanation.definitionFit: One can set up a tent on a site, and a street trader works from a regular spot.

clue.text: Expressed thanks to cast

indicators.note: expressed means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: through, as in through his help, means thanks to

explanation.surface: Someone said thank you to the actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Threw is the past tense of throw, and to cast is to throw.

clue.text: Learned English and Italian, in short

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: short means curt or rude
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone who speaks English and a little Italian is called learned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like 'briefly', but 'in' is the container signal and 'short' means curt.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means scholarly, having much knowledge from study.

clue.text: He'll cover you in certain respects, initially

parts.note: taken as written
certain means sure

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word respects

explanation.surface: A guarantee that someone will protect you, though only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' is insurance cover, the policy that protects you.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriter provides cover against loss, which is protection for the policyholder.

clue.text: Credence Mum's given to fairy

parts.note: mum means keep quiet, and SH is the call for quiet; the 's is the link to the next piece
an elf is a fairy

explanation.surface: A mother puts faith in fairies.
explanation.walkthrough: A credence is a side table or shelf in a church holding the bread and wine; 'Credence' is not belief here.
explanation.definitionFit: A credence is a small side table or ledge beside an altar.

clue.text: Military band bars women — that's wrong

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military band excludes women, which is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians; a SAM BROWNE is an officer's belt with a shoulder strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is a leather belt with a diagonal strap worn by army officers, a band round the waist.
